class Cache
  def initialize(packer: nil)
    @packer = packer
    @store = {}
  end

  def write(key, payload, stale: false)
    if @packer
      serialized = @packer.dump(payload)
    else
      serialized = payload
    end
    @store[key] = { payload: serialized, stale: stale }
  end

  def read(key)
    entry = @store[key]
    return nil unless entry
    
    # If the entry was marked as stale by a previous write, 
    # sweep would have removed it. But read should just return
    # the most recently written payload if it hasn't been swept.
    # Actually, looking at the requirements: "read(key) returns the payload 
    # most recently written under key, or nil if key was never written 
    # or has been removed by #sweep."
    # The sweep removes entries that were written with stale: true.
    # So if an entry is in @store after a sweep, it wasn't stale-written.
    # But wait - what if we write key X with stale: false, then write key X again 
    # with stale: true? After the second write, the entry has stale: true.
    # If no sweep has happened, read should still find it.
    # The requirement says sweep "removes every entry whose #write call passed 
    # stale: true". This implies that after a sweep, entries with stale: true are gone.
    # But what about reading an entry that is currently marked stale (before any sweep)?
    # The description says "most recently written under key, or nil if... has been 
    # removed by #sweep". It doesn't say stale entries can't be read. It says 
    # they will be removed by sweep. So before sweep, they should still be readable.
    
    payload_data = entry[:payload]
    if @packer
      @packer.load(payload_data)
    else
      payload_data
    end
  end

  def sweep
    @store.each_key do |key|
      entry = @store[key]
      if entry[:stale]
        @store.delete(key)
      end
    end
  end
end

    @target = target
  end

  def respond_to?(method_name, include_private = false)
    return true if @target.respond_to?(method_name, include_private)
    super
  end

  def method(name)

  def self.parse(line)
    result = {}
    # Match key="value" patterns where value is anything inside quotes

  def self.squash(text)
    # Ensure we work with a mutable string internally
    # by creating a copy if needed
    str = text.dup

  end
end
